mechanism: Erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism of scopolamine, increasing anticholinergic effects; additive anticholinergic activity enhances CNS and peripheral antimuscarinic effects.
action: Monitor for excessive anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, confusion, tachycardia); consider alternative antibiotic if prolonged scopolamine use; reduce scopolamine dose if interaction suspected.
